Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
An acute, likely IgE-mediated allergic reaction to shellfish (prawn) with features of anaphylaxis: rapid-onset lip angioedema, throat tightness, dyspnoea, dizziness, prior atopy (peanut allergy, asthma). No objective vitals available, but clinical picture warrants emergency management.

Plan during call:
• GP initiated immediate 999 (EMS) call for suspected anaphylaxis.  
• Advised patient to take any available antihistamine while awaiting ambulance.  
• Ensured another person (mother) remained with patient until EMS arrival.  
• Advised post-hospital follow-up for assessment and possible prescription of adrenaline auto-injector (epinephrine pen) and allergy review.

Management Plan
- Immediate transfer to emergency department via ambulance (implemented).  
- Take oral antihistamine on scene if available (implemented).  
- Post-discharge: arrange GP review to discuss anaphylaxis action plan, provision of epinephrine auto-injector, education on allergen avoidance, and referral to allergy/immunology clinic.  
- Review asthma control and ensure inhaler technique and preventive therapy optimized.  
- Document confirmed food allergens in medical record and consider MedicAlert identification.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. IgE-mediated anaphylaxis triggered by shellfish – High likelihood: classic timing, rapid progression, airway symptoms, history of atopy.  
2. Isolated allergic angioedema (non-anaphylactic) – Moderate likelihood: could explain lip swelling but systemic symptoms make this less likely.  
3. Hereditary angioedema – Low likelihood: recurrent swelling possible but food-specific trigger argues against.
